titulo: The factory map: from what you have to the right engine
lead: INEMA has one video engine for each case: explainer, demo, documentary, short, publishing. Picking the wrong engine costs hours. In this lesson you turn the table in the Videos area into a command that tells you which one to use, and you get your machine ready for the next seven lessons.
objetivo: pick the right engine for what you have and what you want, with the Videos area table turned into a command.

aprende.t: The 14 rows of the "Where to start" table in the Videos area
What every engine has in common: a declared input and a gate before the credit
Check git, Python, Node, and FFmpeg before cloning the engines
In which lesson (or sister course) each engine appears

hero_alt: A dark wall with white cards pinned in a flowchart shape, connected by strings that run down to a desk with monitors.

secoes.titulo: From what you have to the engine

nos.detalhe: A topic, your app's link, a reference video, photos, a finished video. It is the first column of the table in the Videos area.
Explainer with an avatar, demo, documentary, 9:16 short, YouTube publishing. The same input leads to different engines depending on the output.
Explicavideos, video-demonstrativo, docflow, refazvideo, MakeShorts, cardshorts, forja-reel, yt-pubx. Each one is a public INEMA repository on GitHub.
Every engine in this course has a point where it would start spending credits or publishing. The practice labs stop there, with the output checked.
The lesson command tells you which lesson of this course covers the engine, or which sibling course owns the topic.

secoes.legenda: The table comes from the INEMA Videos area (eventos.inema.pro/videos/, "Where to start" section), read on 10/19/2026.

secoes.titulo: Three rules that apply to every engine
secoes.sub: They are what makes the factory repeatable.

texto: The engines change every week. The labs clone each one from GitHub and check out an exact commit, the same one the lesson's output was captured from.
When you want the new version, change the commit and run the block again: if the output changes, you know it was the engine.
Each engine reads one file: scenes in JSON, actions.json, a theme in YAML, a script in Markdown. The agent writes that file; the engine does the rest.
Reviewing the file is cheap. Reviewing the finished video is expensive.
Avatar, AI-generated video, and uploading to YouTube sit on the other side of a gate: human approval, a consent form, dry-run mode.
In this course nothing goes past the gate. You learn to get right up to it with everything checked.

exemplo.texto: explicavideos builds scenes and blocks without touching the avatar studio; only the start command generates video, and --help itself warns about that in capital letters.

secoes.sub: Clone the course repository into ~/projetos and check the four tools that every lesson uses.

blocos.conteudo:
for c in git python3 node ffmpeg; do printf "%-8s" "$c"; command -v $c > /dev/null && echo ok || echo FALTA; done
node --version; ffmpeg -version | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1-3; python3 --version

abas.html:
git     ok
python3 ok
node    ok
ffmpeg  ok
v24.13.0
ffmpeg version 6.1.1-3ubuntu5
Python 3.12.3

The versions are the ones on this machine. Any Node 22+ and FFmpeg 6+ will do; the line that matters is ok on all four tools.
Install it with your system's package manager (apt, brew) and run the block again. On Windows, run everything inside WSL: the engines call bash, ffmpeg, and Unix paths.

secoes.titulo: The table turned into a command
secoes.sub: The kit has all 14 rows in qual-motor.py. You pass what you have and what you want; it answers with the engine and the lesson.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-fabrica-v72/kit
python3 "$K/qual-motor.py" --lista | tail -3
python3 "$K/qual-motor.py" tema short; echo "saída: $?"
python3 "$K/qual-motor.py" tema podcast; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
frase         clipe        → musicavideo (fora deste curso (guia da área Vídeos))
video-pronto  publicar     → yt-pubx (aula 8)
14 linhas
Short ou reel 9:16 com gancho
Use: MakeShorts ou cardshorts · aprender: aula 5
saída: 0
SEM MOTOR: com 'tema' a tabela tem: explicativo, documentario, short
saída: 1

A combination that isn't in the table prints SEM MOTOR and exits with code 1, listing what exists for that input. Use --lista to see the 14 rows.

secoes.titulo: The engines in this course and the ones that belong to the siblings
secoes.sub: The map covers more than this course teaches. Follow the right link.

texto: Explicavideos (lesson 2), video-demonstrativo (lesson 3), docflow and refazvideo (lesson 4), MakeShorts and cardshorts (lesson 5), forja-reel (lesson 6), avatar and consent (lesson 7), yt-pubx (lesson 8).
Film with photos and 2.5D camera, and UGC ads: course 2. Brand film from the website: course 5. HyperFrames and Remotion under the hood: course 3.
The 7-step reel, the channel pipeline and the publishing schedule belong to the From chat to agent program: social media on autopilot course.

exercicios.texto: Think of the next video you need to make. Find its line with --lista and ask the map.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: You have the link to your app and want to show how to use it. Which engine?
opcoes: Explicavideos, which starts from a topic and adds an avatar.
docflow, which makes a narrated documentary.
yt-pubx, which publishes the video to YouTube.
perguntas.explica: The line "O link do seu app → Demonstração narrada, clique a clique" points to video-demonstrativo (lesson 3). explicavideos starts from a topic, not from a live app.

perguntas.p: Why do the practices clone each engine at a fixed commit?
opcoes: So the lesson's output stays valid.
Because GitHub only lets you clone old commits from public repositories.
So you don't have to install Python, Node or FFmpeg on the machine.
Because the newest version of every engine spends credits on its own.
perguntas.explica: The engines change every week. With a fixed commit, the block gives the same captured output; if it changes after you switch the commit, the difference came from the engine.

perguntas.p: What is the "gate before credits" in this course?
opcoes: A payment button that each engine shows before it runs.
The point where the engine would spend credits or publish.
A step that only exists in yt-pubx, before the upload.
The memory limit that systemd puts on the render.
perguntas.explica: Avatar, AI-generated video and the YouTube upload sit behind a gate (approval, consent form, dry run mode). The practices get up to it with the output checked, and stop.

perguntas.p: You want a 7-step reel with a publishing schedule. Where do you learn it?
opcoes: In lesson 5 of this course, which covers shorts.
In lesson 8 of this course, which covers publishing.
In course 2 of the program, the production one.
In the social media course of From chat to agent.
perguntas.explica: The 7-step reel and the channel pipeline belong to do-chat-ao-agente-redes-v72. Here, lesson 5 handles only the hook and the quality gate of the short.
